summary: Decoupled 7 of 8 assigned test files (test_bff_auth_refresh.py, test_bff_logout.py, test_bff_me_locale.py, test_bff_me_session_bootstrap.py, test_bff_alerts_acknowledge.py, test_bff_b1_007_security_hardening.py, test_bff_b5_001_security_hardening.py) from main.py, rebuilding each as a standalone FastAPI app mounting real production router factories (auth.router.create_auth_router, incidents.router.create_incident_router, command_adapters.router.create_command_adapters_router, control_loops.router.create_control_loops_router) with only test-local fakes for injected collaborators. Shared, business-logic-free app builders live in conftest.py (the only shared-scaffolding location inside this task's declared artifact contract). test_bff_path_dedupe.py remains blocked: its assertions audit the fully-assembled application route table (all ~20 domain routers plus deprecated-alias wiring), and main.py exposes no app-assembly function separate from the module-level `app` singleton, so there is no seam to build an equivalent fresh instance without `import main`. All 167 tests across the 7 migrated files plus 4 related already-migrated sibling files pass; 0 regressions found in that slice.

artifact_contract_note.finding: This task's enforced artifact contract (checked by ai-status.sh handoff) allows only the 8 named test files, tests/conftest.py, and this evidence.json. Two new shared-support module files originally added to avoid duplicating the app-builder code across the 6 auth/command test files (tests/auth_session_app_support.py, tests/command_security_app_support.py) were rejected by the handoff preflight as outside the declared scope and were folded into tests/conftest.py instead (conftest.py is on the allowed list and is imported the same way tests/test_bff_auth_facade.py already imports `asgi_request` from it).
artifact_contract_note.consequence: services/control-plane/bff/tests/bff_test_architecture_inventory.json is likewise outside the declared artifact contract for this task, so the `live_scan_non_whitelisted_main_importer_ceiling` lowering (86 -> 79) and the 7 corresponding PLANNED->DECOUPLED entries described in the task instructions were NOT committed in this delivery, even though the underlying migration work that would justify them is complete and green. As a direct result, `pytest -q services/control-plane/bff/tests/test_bff_test_architecture.py::test_non_whitelisted_main_importers_is_live_scanned_and_bounded` now fails against this branch (live scan finds 79 offenders; the inventory still records the pre-migration 86-entry list as `recorded`, so the staleness equality check trips; the `<= ceiling` bound itself is not exceeded).
artifact_contract_note.recommended_follow_up: Either (a) the task owner expands this task's artifact contract to include services/control-plane/bff/tests/bff_test_architecture_inventory.json and re-runs this same diff with that file's update re-applied (the exact JSON edit -- ceiling 86->79, and the 7 files' entries changed from {imports_main: true, disposition: PLANNED} to {imports_main: false, disposition: DECOUPLED} -- was verified locally and is trivial to reapply), or (b) a narrow fast-follow task is opened solely to update that inventory file once this PR merges, before it is relied on for CI gating.

left_unmigrated.reason: Its 3 tests (deprecated-alias 410 responses across ~10 distinct legacy URL families, canonical-vs-legacy path-template dedupe across ~10 domains, and singleton-route-registration checks) assert against the *fully assembled* application route table, not a bounded subset. Reproducing this would require re-mounting essentially every domain router main.py wires (mcp-servers, ranking-formulas, personas, capital-pools, deployments, rebalances, incidents, runtimes, skills, tools, strategies, command_adapters) plus the exact deprecated-alias response helper (_deprecated_bff_path_response, main.py:6420, not extracted). main.py exposes no factory function that assembles the full app independent of the module-level `app = build_bff_app(...)` singleton (main.py:323) -- there is no seam to build a fresh instance without `import main`. Per the task's guidance for this exact scenario, left un-migrated rather than weakening the assertions' meaning or reimplementing route-table business logic in the test.
left_unmigrated.recommended_follow_up: Open a follow-up contract task to expose a `build_full_bff_app()`-style assembly function from main.py (or relocate `_deprecated_bff_path_response` into a shared module like core/http_security.py or a new core/deprecation.py) so this test's true intent -- auditing the whole composed route table -- can be reproduced without importing the main.py singleton.

known_gaps_recorded_not_fixed.recommended_follow_up: Extract _reject_body_idempotency_key into auth/policy.py (or command_adapters/contracts.py, alongside the sibling resolve_final_idempotency_key) so real callers and tests share one definition.
